title: A notebook
hook: keep your rule in one place: Pascal kept the record of his night of fire sewn into his coat
tomorrow: the alarm goes off. what reaches you before your feet hit the floor?

segments.voice: Yesterday's line: my honest path. Ruth went deep, Orpah went home, and the book blamed neither. Today the foundations close, and everything gets one place to live.

A scrap of parchment. After the scientist and writer Blaise Pascal died, a servant noticed something stiff in the lining of his coat. Sewn inside was a folded parchment, with a paper copy. His family learned he had carried it for years, unpicking it and sewing it into each new coat he wore. Nobody had known. On it was a date and an hour, late at night. And then, as a heading, one word: Fire.
screen: `SOMETHING STIFF IN THE LINING.` → `SEWN INTO EVERY NEW COAT.` → `NOBODY HAD KNOWN.` → `ONE WORD: FIRE.`

segments.voice: Under it, in short broken lines, Pascal wrote down the night that changed him. God of Abraham, God of Isaac, God of Jacob, not of the philosophers and scholars. Certainty. Certainty. Feeling. Joy. Peace. Joy, joy, joy, tears of joy. It's called his Memorial. Here's the teaching inside it. Pascal was a brilliant mathematician, and what met him that night wasn't a proof. It was, in his words, the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, the living God of the Bible, met in person, as Christian faith holds God can be. And he didn't trust himself to remember it. So he wrote it down, once, in one place, and kept that place against his body. That's what a notebook is for. This whole stretch has been building a rule: my own, a little rule, five words, my why, already here, one gap, small and real, my honest path. Scattered, they fade. Kept together, in one notebook you can find, they become something you can return to on the morning you've forgotten all of it. Pascal's page was small enough to sew into a coat. Yours can be small too. Tomorrow, the daily practice begins, at the very top of the day.
screen: `FIRE.` · `NOT THE GOD OF THE PHILOSOPHERS.` · `WRITTEN ONCE, KEPT CLOSE.` · `A RULE IN ONE PLACE.` · then, large: `ONE NOTEBOOK.`

segments.voice: Take a notebook, any notebook, and write on its first page by hand: my rule. Under it, copy the lines from these foundations that you want to keep, five words, my why, one gap, small and real, my honest path, in your own handwriting. Leave the rest of the page empty for now.
A notebook: one place where your rule lives, kept close, the way Pascal kept his Memorial sewn into his coat.
Keep this: one notebook, kept close like Pascal's page in the coat. The foundations are laid.
